questions.stem: An architect's brief asks why five-membered chelate rings are preferred over four- or six-membered rings?

options.text: They balance ring strain and entropy loss

questions.explanation: Five-membered rings minimise ring strain while keeping entropy loss small. Four-membered rings are strained and six-membered rings lose more entropy.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.topic: CFSE of a low-spin d6 octahedral ion
questions.learningObjective: Explain low-spin d6 CFSE
questions.stem: An architect's note asks why low-spin d6 has CFSE = -2.4 Delta_o

answer.exemplar: All six electrons occupy the lower t2g orbitals, so CFSE = 6(-0.4 Delta_o) = -2.4 Delta_o, the maximum stabilisation for d6.

questions.explanation: t2g^6 gives -2.4 Delta_o. High-spin would give -0.4.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.topic: CFSE of a high-spin d6 octahedral ion
questions.learningObjective: Explain high-spin d6 CFSE
questions.stem: An architect's note asks why high-spin d6 has CFSE = -0.4 Delta_o

answer.exemplar: High-spin d6 has t2g^4 eg^2, so CFSE = 4(-0.4) + 2(0.6) = -0.4 Delta_o, a small stabilisation because two electrons occupy eg.

questions.explanation: Two eg electrons reduce stabilisation. Low-spin would give -2.4.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.topic: CFSE of a d3 octahedral ion
questions.learningObjective: Explain d3 CFSE
questions.stem: An architect's note asks why d3 has CFSE = -1.2 Delta_o

answer.exemplar: A d3 ion fills three t2g orbitals singly, giving CFSE = 3(-0.4 Delta_o) = -1.2 Delta_o with no pairing energy.

questions.explanation: Three t2g electrons give -1.2 Delta_o. No pairing is needed.
